claim: Gastrulation is a fundamental process in organism development, leading to the establishment of the embryonic germ layers (endoderm, mesoderm and ectoderm) and the basic organization of the body plan.
source: Gastrulation is a fundamental process in organism development, leading to the establishment of the embryonic germ layers (endoderm, mesoderm and ectoderm) and the basic organization of the body plan.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about gastrulation.

claim: In vertebrates, gastrulation proceeds through evolutionary conserved morphogenetic movements, including the spreading of blastoderm cells (epiboly), the internalization of mesoderm and endoderm, convergent movements towards the prospective dorsal side and extension along the antero-posterior axis (convergence and extension, respectively).
source: Although in vertebrates early embryonic development has adopted highly diverse configurations, gastrulation proceeds through evolutionary conserved morphogenetic movements, including the spreading of blastoderm cells (epiboly), the internalization of mesoderm and endoderm, convergent movements towards the prospective dorsal side and extension along the antero-posterior axis (convergence and extension, respectively) (Solnica-Krezel, 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Solnica-Krezel, 2005.

claim: The induction of the embryonic organizer in the prospective dorsal side occurs downstream of earlier developmental events, which are driven by maternal determinants deposited in the oocyte during maturation in the ovaries.
source: In fishes and amphibians, the induction of the embryonic organizer in the prospective dorsal side occurs downstream of earlier developmental events, which are driven by maternal determinants deposited in the oocyte during maturation in the ovaries (Kelly et al., 2000; Nojima et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 1998a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Kelly et al., 2000; Nojima et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 1998a.

claim: The prechordal plate is key for the patterning of the forebrain through the regulated secretion of morphogens including sonic hedgehog (shh), Fibroblast growth factors (fgf), and inhibitors of the Wingless-Int (Wnt) pathway, such as dickkopf1b (dkk1b) and secreted frizzled-related proteins (sFRP).
source: The prechordal plate is key for the patterning of the forebrain, which it affects through the regulated secretion of morphogens including sonic hedgehog (shh), Fibroblast growth factors (fgf), and inhibitors of the Wingless-Int (Wnt) pathway, such as dickkopf1b (dkk1b) and secreted frizzled-related proteins (sFRP).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the role of the prechordal plate in forebrain patterning.

claim: The prechordal plate is required for the sequential patterning of forebrain elements along its rostral migration.
source: Along its rostral migration, the prechordal plate is required for the sequential patterning of forebrain elements (García-Calero et al., 2008; Puelles and Rubenstein, 2015), demonstrating a temporal and spatial requirement for this migratory cell population for brain development from gastrulation onwards.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to García-Calero et al., 2008; Puelles and Rubenstein, 2015.

claim: Astyanax mexicanus exists in two different eco-morphotypes: a 'wild type' river-dwelling fish (surface fish) and several geographically isolated troglomorphic populations (cavefish) that live in total and permanent darkness.
source: This species exists in two different eco-morphotypes that are distributed in Central and North America: a 'wild type' river-dwelling fish (surface fish) and several geographically isolated troglomorphic populations (cavefish) that live in total and permanent darkness (Mitchell et al., 1977; Elliott, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Mitchell et al., 1977; Elliott, 2018.

claim: Cavefish lack eyes and pigmentation.
source: Fish from the cave morphotype can be easily identified because they lack eyes and pigmentation.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the phenotype of cavefish.

claim: Cavefish have evolved mechanisms of sensory compensation, such as enhanced chemosensory and mechanosensory sensibilities.
source: As a result of the absence of visual information, the cavefish has evolved mechanisms of sensory compensation, such as enhanced chemosensory and mechanosensory sensibilities (Hinaux et al., 2016; Yoshizawa et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Hinaux et al., 2016; Yoshizawa et al., 2010.

claim: Behavioral changes in cavefish are associated with morphological modifications such as larger olfactory sensory organs, increased number of facial mechanosensory neuromasts and taste buds, and modified serotonergic and orexinergic neurotransmission systems.
source: Such behavioral changes are associated with morphological modifications such as larger olfactory sensory organs (Blin et al., 2018; Hinaux et al., 2016), increased number of facial mechanosensory neuromasts (Yoshizawa et al., 2014) and taste buds (Varatharasan et al., 2009), and modified serotonergic and orexinergic neurotransmission systems (Alié et al., 2018; Elipot et al., 2014a; Jaggard et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to Blin et al., 2018; Hinaux et al., 2016; Yoshizawa et al., 2014; Varatharasan et al., 2009; Alié et al., 2018; Elipot et al., 2014a; Jaggard et al., 2018.

claim: Morphological and behavioral adaptations in cavefish have arisen mainly due to heterotopic and heterochronic differences in the expression of signaling molecules from midline organizers at the end of gastrulation.
source: Remarkably, such morphological and behavioral adaptations have a developmental origin, and have arisen mainly due to heterotopic and heterochronic differences in the expression of signaling molecules from midline organizers at the end of gastrulation, specifically at the 'neural plate' or bud stage.
evidence: This is a statement about the developmental origin of cavefish adaptations.

claim: Subtle differences in the shh and fgf8 expression domains, which are respectively larger and earlier in cavefish compared to surface fish, affect downstream processes of gene expression, morphogenetic movements during neurulation and cell differentiation, driving the developmental evolution of the cavefish nervous system.
source: Subtle differences in the shh and fgf8 expression domains, which are respectively larger and earlier in cavefish compared to surface fish, affect downstream processes of gene expression, morphogenetic movements during neurulation and cell differentiation, driving the developmental evolution of the cavefish nervous system (Hinaux et al., 2016; Menuet et al., 2007; Pottin et al., 2011; Ren et al., 2018; Yamamoto et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Hinaux et al., 2016; Menuet et al., 2007; Pottin et al., 2011; Ren et al., 2018; Yamamoto et al., 2004.

claim: In surface fish at 50% epiboly, dkk1b expression was observed at the dorsal margin in two groups of cells separated by a gap in the center in around 70% of embryos.
source: In the surface fish, dkk1b expression was observed at the dorsal margin in two groups of cells separated by a gap in the center (Figure 1A), a pattern observed in the majority of the embryos (around 70%; Figure 1C blue).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1A and quantified in Figure 1C.

claim: In cavefish at 50% epiboly, dkk1b expression showed a single central spot of variable extension in around 70% of embryos.
source: In the cavefish, a single central spot of variable extension (Figure 1B) was observed in most of the samples analyzed (around 70%; Figure 1C red).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1B and quantified in Figure 1C.

claim: In cavefish at 50% epiboly, dkk1b+ cells were already internalized under the dorsal aspect of the margin, revealing a precocious internalization process when compared to surface fish.
source: In cavefish at 50% epiboly, the dkk1b+ cells were already internalized under the dorsal aspect of the margin (Figure 1D–D'' and E,E'), revealing a precocious internalization process when compared to that in surface fish.
evidence: This statement is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 1D-D'' and E,E'.

claim: In surface fish embryos at 50% epiboly, chordin expression extended more ventrally than in cavefish.
source: In surface fish embryos, chordin expression extended more ventrally than in cavefish (Figure 1F–H), as quantified by measuring the angle of expression in an animal view (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1F-H and quantified in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The difference in chordin pattern extension suggested that convergence towards the dorsal pole was more advanced in cavefish.
source: This difference in chordin pattern extension suggested that convergence towards the dorsal pole was more advanced in cavefish.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the chordin expression data.

claim: At 50% epiboly, no significant differences were observed in the vegetal-animal extension of lefty1 expression between surface fish and cavefish.
source: The ventro-dorsal extension of lefty1 expression was similarly variable in both morphotypes at this stage (not shown) and no significant differences were observed in the vegetal-animal extension of lefty1 expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: At 50% epiboly, the homeobox gene flh showed localized expression in the dorsal margin without differences in width nor in height when compared between morphotypes.
source: At 50% epiboly, the homeobox gene flh showed localized expression in the dorsal margin (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D–E), without differences in width nor in height when compared between morphotypes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D-F.

claim: At 50% epiboly, ntl and bra expression extended homogenously all around the margin (blastopore) with no differences observed between surface fish and cavefish.
source: At the same stage, ntl and bra expression extended homogenously all around the margin (blastopore), hindering the identification of the prospective dorsal side (Figure 1—figure supplement 2G,H and I,J). No differences were observed between surface fish and cavefish.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2G-J.

claim: In zebrafish, dkk1b is expressed in two spots in the embryonic organizer.
source: In zebrafish, dkk1b is expressed in two spots in the embryonic organizer (Hashimoto et al., 2000) similarly to the surface fish condition (Figure 1A), although the gap is less pronounced in zebrafish.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hashimoto et al., 2000.

claim: At 70% epiboly in surface fish, the two clusters of dkk1b expression observed at 50% epiboly began to coalesce at the midline.
source: In surface fish, the two clusters observed at 50% epiboly began to coalesce at the midline at 70% epiboly (Figure 2A)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: At 70% epiboly in cavefish, dkk1b-expressing cells became grouped dorsally and the leading cells were more advanced towards the animal pole compared to surface fish.
source: whereas in cavefish, dkk1b-expressing cells became grouped dorsally and the leading cells were more advanced towards the animal pole (arrow in Figure 2B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: At 80% epiboly in cavefish, dkk1b+ cells were close to their final position in the anterior prechordal plate at the rostral end of the embryonic axis.
source: At 80% epiboly, dkk1b+ cells in the cavefish were close to their final position in the anterior prechordal plate at the rostral end of the embryonic axis (arrow Figure 2E).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: At 80% epiboly in surface fish, leading cells expressing dkk1b had reached a similar distance as those in cavefish at 70% epiboly.
source: At the same stage, leading cells expressing dkk1b in the surface fish (arrow Figure 2D) had reached a similar distance as those in cavefish at 70% epiboly (compare values in Figure 2F and C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2D, 2F, and 2C.

claim: At 70% epiboly, chordin, lefty1, and ntl showed a greater height value for their expression domain in cavefish than in surface fish embryos.
source: The same analysis was performed at 70% epiboly for the markers chordin (Figure 2G–I), lefty1 (Figure 2J–L) and ntl (Figure 2M–O). These three genes showed a greater height value for their expression domain in cavefish than in surface fish embryos.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2G-O.

claim: At equivalent stages during gastrulation, anteroposterior axis formation is more advanced in cavefish.
source: This further suggested that at equivalent stages during gastrulation, anteroposterior axis formation is more advanced in cavefish.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the gene expression data.

claim: At 70% and 80% epiboly, the height value of myoD expression domain was higher in cavefish embryos than in surface fish embryos.
source: The height value of the expression domain was higher in cavefish embryos, at both at 70% and 80% epiboly, than in surface fish embryos (Figure 3E)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: At 70% and 80% epiboly, the central/dorsal non-expressing zone for myoD was wider in the surface fish than in cavefish.
source: whereas the central/dorsal non-expressing zone was wider in the surface fish at both stages (Figure 3F).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: For msgn1, no significant differences were found in the height values at 70% and 80% epiboly between surface fish and cavefish.
source: For msgn1, no significant differences were found in the height values at 70% and 80% epiboly (Figure 3K)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3K.

claim: At 80% epiboly, the dorsal non-expressing zone for msgn1 was reduced in cavefish embryos compared to surface fish.
source: but similarly to what was observed for myoD, the dorsal non-expressing zone was reduced in cavefish embryos at 80% epiboly (Figure 3L).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3L.

claim: The differences observed in paraxial mesoderm extension were mainly due to the expression of myoD (but not msgn1) in the cell population, which is more advanced towards the animal end of the embryo.
source: These results suggested that the differences observed in our measurements of paraxial mesoderm extension were mainly due to the expression of myoD (but not msgn1) in the cell population, which is more advanced towards the animal end of the embryo (Figure 3N, P).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the double ISH data shown in Figure 3M-P.

claim: The size of the central zone where expression of the two paraxial markers is interrupted suggests an earlier convergence and extension in cavefish than in surface fish.
source: In addition, if the size of the central zone where expression of the two paraxial markers is interrupted is taken as readout of dorsal convergence, these data also suggest an earlier convergence and extension in cavefish than in surface fish (at a given stage of epiboly).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the paraxial mesoderm marker data.

claim: In A. mexicanus at bud stage, three non-overlapping molecular subdomains were recognized in the axial mesoderm: the anterior prechordal plate or polster labeled by dkk1b, the posterior prechordal plate defined by shh expression, and the notochord more posteriorly, labeled by ntl.
source: Using triple fluorescent in situ hybridization, three non-overlapping molecular subdomains were recognized: the anterior prechordal plate or polster labeled by dkk1b, the posterior prechordal plate defined by shh expression (wider in cavefish as previously described; Pottin et al., 2011; Yamamoto et al., 2004) and the notochord more posteriorly, labeled by ntl (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: The posterior prechordal plate is wider in cavefish as previously described.
source: the posterior prechordal plate defined by shh expression (wider in cavefish as previously described; Pottin et al., 2011; Yamamoto et al., 2004)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Pottin et al., 2011; Yamamoto et al., 2004.

claim: lefty1 expression covered both the anterior and posterior subdomains of the prechordal plate.
source: In addition, lefty1 expression covered both the anterior and posterior subdomains of the prechordal plate (Figure 4C–F).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4C-F.

claim: In the posterior prechordal plate, lefty1 and shh showed overlapping patterns in both morphotypes.
source: In the posterior prechordal plate, lefty1 and shh showed overlapping patterns in both morphotypes (Figure 4C,D)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: dkk1b and lefty1 showed only minimal co-expression anteriorly.
source: whereas dkk1b and lefty1 showed only minimal co-expression anteriorly (Figure 4E,F)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4E,F.

claim: The distribution of polster dkk1b-expressing cells was strikingly different between the two morphs: in surface fish, they were tightly compacted, whereas in cavefish, they were loosely organized.
source: Moreover, the distribution of polster dkk1b-expressing cells was strikingly different between the two morphs. In surface fish, they were tightly compacted (Figure 4A), whereas in cavefish, they were loosely organized (Figure 4B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: The numbers of dkk1b-expressing cells were similar in cavefish and surface fish.
source: The numbers of dkk1b-expressing cells, analyzed in confocal sections, were similar in cavefish and surface fish (Figure 4G).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The distribution of the dkk1b cells in the antero-posterior axis was identical between cavefish and surface fish.
source: The distribution of the dkk1b cells in the antero-posterior axis, measured by the distance between the first and the last cells (Length A-P), was identical (Figure 4H).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: The dkk1b-positive cells covered a larger extension in the lateral axis in cavefish embryos, indicating that these cells are arranged at a lower density than in surface fish.
source: However, the dkk1b-positive cells covered a larger extension in the lateral axis (Length lateral) in cavefish embryos (Figure 4I), indicating that these cells are arranged at a lower density than in surface fish.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Both the anterior/polster (dkk1b+) and the posterior part (shh+) of the prechordal plate are laterally expanded in cavefish.
source: Thus, both the anterior/polster (dkk1b+) and the posterior part (shh+) of the prechordal plate are laterally expanded in cavefish.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the data presented.

claim: The distance from the anterior-most polster cell expressing dkk1b to the leading notochord cell expressing ntl was identical in the two morphs.
source: The distance from the anterior-most polster cell expressing dkk1b to the leading notochord cell expressing ntl was identical in the two morphs (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: Polster cells expressing dkk1b laid just beneath the cells of the anterior neural plate border (dlx3b+) in both morphotypes.
source: Polster cells expressing dkk1b laid just beneath the cells of the anterior neural plate border (dlx3b+) in both morphotypes (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D,E).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2D,E.

claim: At bud stage, for the three notochord markers (ntl, bra, and flh), the distance from the rostral expression boundary to the tail bud (normalized by the size of the embryo) was larger in cavefish than in surface fish.
source: For the three notochord markers, the distance from the rostral expression boundary to the tail bud (normalized by the size of the embryo) was larger in cavefish than in surface fish (Figure 4N–P).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4N-P.

claim: The observations of axial and paraxial mesoderm markers during mid-gastrulation suggest a precocious convergence and extension in cavefish when compared to surface fish.
source: In line with our observations of axial and paraxial mesoderm markers during mid-gastrulation (Figures 2–3), these results suggest a precocious convergence and extension in cavefish when compared to surface fish.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figures 2-4.

claim: In zebrafish embryos, dkk1b expression in the prechordal plate becomes downregulated from early somitogenesis.
source: In zebrafish embryos, dkk1b expression in the prechordal plate becomes downregulated from early somitogenesis (Hashimoto et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hashimoto et al., 2000.

claim: In surface fish, dkk1b was still expressed in all embryos at the 6- and 8-somite stage.
source: In surface fish, dkk1b was still expressed in all embryos at the 6- and 8-somite stage (13/13 [not shown] and 17/17 [Figures 5A and 6E, right]).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figures 5A and 6E.

claim: In cavefish, dkk1b expression was observed only in 46% of the embryos at the 6-somite stage and it was absent in 64% of embryos at the 8-somite stage.
source: By contrast, in cavefish, dkk1b expression was observed only in 46% of the embryos at the 6-somite stage (6/13, always with low signal level; not shown) and it was absent in 64% of embryos at the 8-somite stage (21/33, Figures 5B and 6E right).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figures 5B and 6E.

claim: At 50% epiboly, dkk1b transcript levels were similar in the two morphs.
source: At 50% epiboly, dkk1b transcript levels were similar in the two morphs (0.95 fold, NS)
evidence: This statement is based on qPCR data.

claim: At bud stage, dkk1b levels were almost four times lower in cavefish than in surface fish embryos.
source: but at bud stage, dkk1b levels were almost four times lower in cavefish than in surface fish embryos (0.27 fold).
evidence: This statement is based on qPCR data.

claim: LiCl treatments (0.1M and 0.2M, from 8 to 13 hpf) in surface fish produced a decrease of the size of the optic vesicle at 13 hpf and a reduction of the size of the retina and lens at 24 hpf.
source: In line with results reported in zebrafish (Shinya et al., 2000), LiCl treatments (0.1M and 0.2M, from 8 to 13 hpf) in surface fish produced a decrease of the size of the optic vesicle at 13 hpf (not shown) and a reduction of the size of the retina and lens at 24 hpf (Figure 5D–F,H,I), which are hallmarks of cavefish embryonic eye morphology (Yamamoto et al., 2004); compare to Figure 5G).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5D-I and citations to Shinya et al., 2000 and Yamamoto et al., 2004.

claim: Manipulation of the levels of Wnt-βcat signaling in surface fish produced a misshaped retina with a wider optic stalk, observed in 41% and 50% of the examined eyes of embryos treated with LiCl 0.1M and 0.2M, respectively.
source: In addition, manipulation of the levels of Wnt-βcat signaling in surface fish produced a misshaped retina with a wider optic stalk (Figure 5F). This was observed in 41% and 50% of the examined eyes of embryos treated with LiCl 0.1M and 0.2M, respectively (Figure 5J).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5F,J.

claim: The expression domain of the optic stalk marker pax2a was significantly wider at 36 hpf in surface fish embryos exposed to LiCL and in cavefish embryos than in untreated surface fish embryos.
source: The interpretation of this morphological coloboma-like phenotype was confirmed molecularly, as the expression domain of the optic stalk marker pax2a was significantly wider at 36 hpf in surface fish embryos exposed to LiCL and in cavefish embryos than in untreated surface fish embryos (Figure 5K–N,O).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5K-O.

claim: Modified levels of Wnt signaling during early embryogenesis might contribute to the developmental evolution of cavefish eye defects.
source: Together these data strongly suggest that modified levels of Wnt signaling during early embryogenesis might contribute to the developmental evolution of cavefish eye defects.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the LiCl treatment experiments.

claim: At 50% epiboly, the percentages of each of the phenotypic categories present in hybrid embryos were strikingly similar to those of their maternal morphotypes.
source: At 50% epiboly, the percentages each of the phenotypic categories (described in Figure 1A–C) present in hybrid embryos were strikingly similar to those of their maternal morphotypes, with the majority of HybSF presenting two spots of dkk1b expression like surface fish embryos, whereas most of HybCF embryos showed only one continuous expression domain (Figure 6B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: At 70% epiboly, the advancement of axial mesoderm populations labeled by dkk1b was significantly increased in HybCF compared to HybSF, with height values akin to those of their respective maternal morphs.
source: At 70% epiboly, the results followed the same trend. In HybSF embryos, the two domains of dkk1b-expressing cells begin to join dorsally, with little advancement towards the animal pole, as in surface embryos (Figure 6C). By contrast, HybCF were more like cavefish embryos, with cells grouped dorsally close to the animal end (Figure 6C). Analyses of the distance reached by the leading cell showed significant differences between the two reciprocal hybrids types, which were identical to their maternal morphs (Figure 6C, right).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The advancement of axial mesoderm populations labeled by lefty1 and ntl at 70% epiboly was significantly increased in HybCF compared to HybSF, with height values akin to those of their respective maternal morphs.
source: The expression of lefty1 and ntl at 70% epiboly was also examined in F1 hybrids (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B, respectively). The advancement of axial mesoderm populations labeled by the two markers was significantly increased in HybCF compared to HybSF, with height values akin to those of their respective maternal morphs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B, right).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Spatio-temporal differences observed during gastrulation between cavefish and surface fish fully depend on maternal contribution.
source: These results indicate that spatio-temporal differences observed during gastrulation between cavefish and surface fish fully depend on maternal contribution.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the F1 hybrid data.

claim: A broader distribution of dkk1b-expressing cells was found in the HybCF than in the HybSF at the end of gastrulation.
source: We found a broader distribution of dkk1b-expressing cells in the HybCF (Figure 6D, center bottom) than in the HybSF (Figure 6D, left bottom).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The patterns of dkk1b expression observed in the F1 hybrids at the end of gastrulation were identical to those patterns in their maternal morphs.
source: The patterns observed in the F1 hybrids were identical those patterns in their maternal morphs (Figure 6D, right), highlighting the effect of the oocyte composition up to the end of gastrulation, well after the activation of the zygotic genome.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: At the 8-somite stage, the downregulation of dkk1b expression is still under the influence of maternal factors, although this influence is weaker than at earlier stages.
source: We concluded that at the 8-somite stage the downregulation of dkk1b expression is still under the influence of maternal factors, although this influence is weaker than at earlier stages.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the F1 hybrid data at the 8-somite stage.

claim: Lens size at 24 hpf, 2 dpf, and 3 dpf was identical in reciprocal F1 hybrids, showing intermediate sizes between parental values.
source: The difference in lens size between surface fish and cavefish was significant, as expected, and increased as development proceeds (in cavefish: −42% at 24 hpf; −66% at 2 dpf; and −84% at 3 dpf), following the regressive process in one morph and the growth process in the other (Figure 7A–D). However, at all three stages, lens size was identical in reciprocal F1 hybrids, showing intermediate sizes between parental values (Figure 7A–D).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7A-D.

claim: Lens size is not under maternal control.
source: This suggests that lens size is not under maternal control.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the F1 hybrid lens size data.

claim: The size of the olfactory placodes shows no evidence of maternal influence in reciprocal F1 hybrids at 24 hpf.
source: Of note, the size of the olfactory placodes, which is inversely correlated to the size of lens placodes in the two Astyanax morphs (Hinaux et al., 2016), also shows no evidence of maternal influence in reciprocal F1 hybrids at 24 hpf (Figure 7—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and a citation to Hinaux et al., 2016.

claim: The developmental trade-off between the lens and olfactory placodes is not maternally controlled.
source: suggesting that the developmental trade-off between the two placodal sensory derivatives is not maternally controlled.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the F1 hybrid data for lens and olfactory placode sizes.

claim: HybSF and HybCF were indistinguishable for the number of Caspase3-positive apoptotic cells in the lenses at 2 dpf and 3 dpf, both showing values closer to those of surface fish than to those of cavefish.
source: HybSF and HybCF were indistinguishable, both showing ~2.5 apoptotic cells per 104 µm3 at 2 dpf and ~1 apoptotic cell per 103 µm3 at 3 dpf (Figure 7E and F). These values were closer to those of surface fish than to those of cavefish values, indicating a dominant effect of surface alleles in heterozygotes (Figure 7E and F, right).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7E and F.

claim: The exact same pattern of dominant surface allele effect was observed for Caspase3-positive cells in the 3 dpf retina.
source: The exact same pattern was observed for Caspase3-positive cells in the 3 dpf retina (Figure 7A and G).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7A and G.

claim: The eye degenerative process that is associated with and triggered by lens apoptosis is not maternally controlled in cavefish.
source: These results show that the eye degenerative process that is associated with and triggered by lens apoptosis is not maternally controlled in cavefish.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the F1 hybrid apoptosis data.

claim: The width of the Shh expression domain in the prechordal plate at 10 hpf was identical in HybSF and HybCF.
source: Strikingly, and contrarily to the Dkk1b phenotype shown above, the width of the Shh expression domain in the prechordal plate at 10 hpf was identical in HybSF and HybCF (Figure 7H and I)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7H and I.

claim: There is a lack of maternal contribution to the control of Shh expression.
source: suggesting a lack of maternal contribution to the control of Shh expression, in line with the lack of maternal control on the downstream degenerative phenotype.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the F1 hybrid Shh expression data.

claim: As regards the size of the optic fissure, HybSF and HybCF were significantly different, indicating a maternal genetic effect on this phenotype.
source: As regards the size of the optic fissure, HybSF and HybCF were significantly different, indicating a maternal genetic effect on this phenotype, and both were closer to the surface fish values (Figure 7K), suggesting a partial dominance of the surface fish zygotic program.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7K.

claim: The maternal control of gastrulation has long-lasting consequences for morphological evolution.
source: Together with the above results showing that Dkk1b expression in the prechordal plate is maternally controlled (Figure 6), and that manipulation of the Wnt signaling pathway in surface fish mimics the cavefish coloboma (Figure 5), these data show how the maternal control of gastrulation has long-lasting consequences for morphological evolution.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined data from Figures 5, 6, and 7.

claim: For Lhx9 and Lhx7, hybrids values were similar and intermediate between those of the cave and surface morphs, with a slight deviation towards the surface morph more evident for the HybSF.
source: For Lhx9 and Lhx7, hybrids values were similar and intermediate between those of the cave and surface morphs, with a slight deviation towards the surface morph more evident for the HybSF (Figure 8A and B, center and right).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 8A and B.

claim: A significant difference in Hypocretin neuron numbers existed between reciprocal hybrids, suggesting an involvement of maternal components.
source: For the Hypocretin and NPY neuropeptidergic lineages that are derived from Lhx9- and Lhx7-expressing progenitors, respectively, a significant difference in neuron numbers existed between reciprocal hybrids (Figure 8C and D), suggesting an involvement of maternal components.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 8C and D.

claim: The number of Hypocretin neurons in HybSF and the number of NPY neurons in HybCF were identical to those in their maternal morphotype.
source: Moreover, the number of Hypocretin neurons in HybSF and the number of NPY neurons in HybCF were identical those in their maternal morphotype, whereas values for their reciprocal hybrids were close to the theoretical intermediate value (Figure 8C and D, on the right).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 8C and D.

claim: Maternal determinants impact hypothalamic neuronal differentiation, possibly together with other, complex, allelic dominance or zygotic mechanisms.
source: These results suggest that maternal determinants impact hypothalamic neuronal differentiation, possibly together with other, complex, allelic dominance or zygotic mechanisms.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the F1 hybrid hypothalamic neuron data.

claim: The effect of maternal determinants are fully penetrant up until the final stages of gastrulation.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that the effect of maternal determinants are fully penetrant up until the final stages of gastrulation, suggesting that RNAs and proteins that are present in the oocyte must vary between the two Astyanax morphotypes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the F1 hybrid data across developmental stages.

claim: At later stages, the maternal effect appears to be 'diluted' by other mechanisms that regulate gene expression and morphogenesis, but some important differences can still be observed between reciprocal F1 hybrids.
source: At later stages, the maternal effect appears to be 'diluted' by other mechanisms that regulate gene expression and morphogenesis, but some important differences can still be observed between reciprocal F1 hybrids, highlighting how maternal influence translates into later morphological phenotypes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the F1 hybrid data at later developmental stages.

claim: The sample-to-sample distance analysis grouped the four types of samples into two clear categories, strictly depending on their maternal contribution.
source: The sample-to-sample distance analysis grouped the four types of samples into two clear categories, strictly depending on their maternal contribution (Figure 9A).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Principal component analyses (PCA) analyses clustered the samples from hybrid embryos together with those from their maternal morphotype.
source: Similarly, principal component analyses (PCA) analyses clustered the samples from hybrid embryos together with those from their maternal morphotype (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Among the 20,730 genes that were expressed at the 2-cell stage, close to a third (32%) were differentially expressed between surface and cavefish.
source: Among the 20,730 genes that were expressed at the 2-cell stage, close to a third (32%) were differentially expressed between surface and cavefish (Figure 9B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: A similar proportion of genes was up- or downregulated in cavefish relative to surface fish (17.25% and 14.69%, respectively).
source: A similar proportion was up- or downregulated in cavefish relative to surface fish (17.25% and 14.69%, respectively).
evidence: This statement is based on the RNA-seq data analysis.

claim: Cell adhesion (7.1%) and signaling (6.5%) were among the significantly enriched biological processes in DEGs with an absolute fold change higher than 5.
source: Cell adhesion (7.1%) and signaling (6.5%) were among the significantly enriched biological processes that might be most relevant for this work (Figure 9C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 9C.

claim: Genes that are involved in ion transport, cell adhesion and cell signaling are mainly upregulated in cavefish eggs compared to surface fish eggs.
source: This means that genes that are involved in ion transport, cell adhesion and cell signaling are mainly upregulated in cavefish eggs compared to surface fish eggs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the GO enrichment analysis.

claim: The RNA composition of the cavefish and surface fish eggs shows a strong maternal signature.
source: Together, these results show that the RNA composition of the cavefish and surface fish eggs shows a strong maternal signature, and thus that oocyte content could contribute to the developmental evolution of cavefish phenotype.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the RNA-seq data.

claim: Vsx1 and Oep mRNA levels were significantly reduced in cavefish (2.50 and 1.75 times lower expression in cavefish, respectively) as confirmed by qPCR analyses on 2 hpf embryos.
source: qPCR analyses on 2 hpf embryos showed that Vsx1 and Oep mRNA levels were significantly reduced in cavefish (2.50 and 1.75 times lower expression in cavefish, respectively) confirming the RNA-seq results (8.21 and 1.63 times lower expression, respectively).
evidence: This statement is based on qPCR data that confirms RNA-seq results.

claim: Vsx1-injected and Oep-injected cavefish embryos were similar to control cavefish embryos in terms of their spatio-temporal dkk1b pattern.
source: Vsx1-injected and Oep-injected embryos were similar to control cavefish embryos in terms of their spatio-temporal dkk1b pattern, although some signs of disorganization were visible on several specimens (not shown).
evidence: This statement is based on overexpression experiments.

claim: A role for Vsx1 and Oep maternal transcripts in the variations of dkk1b expression observed between the two Astyanax morphs is unlikely.
source: Thus, a role for Vsx1 and Oep maternal transcripts in the variations of dkk1b expression observed between the two Astyanax morphs is unlikely.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the overexpression experiments.

claim: In A. mexicanus, the expression of shh in the posterior prechordal plate occupies a wider domain in the cavefish than in the surface fish.
source: In A. mexicanus, the expression of shh in the posterior prechordal plate occupies a wider domain in the cavefish than in the surface fish (Pottin et al., 2011; Yamamoto et al., 2004)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Pottin et al., 2011; Yamamoto et al., 2004.

claim: Enhanced shh signaling has pleiotropic effects in the development of head structures in the cavefish.
source: and enhanced shh signaling has pleiotropic effects in the development of head structures in the cavefish (Yamamoto et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Yamamoto et al., 2009.

claim: The anterior domain of the prechordal plate is a source of the morphogen dkk1b, whose expression is complementary to that of shh at the neural plate stage.
source: Here, we showed that the anterior domain of the prechordal plate is a source of the morphogen dkk1b, whose expression is complementary to that of shh at the neural plate stage (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: At the neural plate stage, dkk1b-expressing cells are organized as a compact cluster in surface fish, whereas in cavefish they are more loosely distributed, and with lower levels of dkk1b transcripts.
source: At this stage, dkk1b-expressing cells are organized as a compact cluster in surface fish, whereas in cavefish they are more loosely distributed, and with lower levels of dkk1b transcripts.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings presented earlier in the manuscript.

claim: Mouse or Xenopus embryos with impaired Dkk1 function lack anterior brain structures.
source: Mouse or Xenopus embryos with impaired Dkk1 function lack anterior brain structures (Glinka et al., 1998; Mukhopadhyay et al., 2001)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Glinka et al., 1998; Mukhopadhyay et al., 2001.

claim: Misexpression of dkk1b in zebrafish embryos produces anteriorization of the neurectoderm, including enlargement of eyes.
source: whereas misexpression of dkk1b in zebrafish embryos produces anteriorization of the neurectoderm, including enlargement of eyes (Shinya et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Shinya et al., 2000.

claim: Head development is sensitive to Wnt signaling dosage.
source: Head development is sensitive to Wnt signaling dosage (Lewis et al., 2008)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Lewis et al., 2008.

claim: The temporal variations of dkk1b expression might contribute to forebrain evolution in cavefish.
source: and the temporal variations of dkk1b expression that we observed here might contribute to forebrain evolution in cavefish.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the dkk1b expression data and the LiCl experiments.

claim: The timing and intensity of Wnt and Bmp signaling at the anterior pole of the axial mesoderm must instruct the fate and morphogenetic movements of overlying anterior neural plate progenitors.
source: Indeed, the timing and intensity of Wnt (this work) and Bmp (Hinaux et al., 2016) signaling at the anterior pole of the axial mesoderm must instruct the fate and morphogenetic movements of overlying anterior neural plate progenitors that are destined to form the optic region and the hypothalamus, as well as the placode derivatives (Bielen et al., 2017; Rétaux et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Hinaux et al., 2016; Bielen et al., 2017; Rétaux et al., 2013.

claim: The differences observed in the axial mesoderm of A. mexicanus morphotypes may be the consequence of upstream events during gastrulation.
source: We hypothesized that the differences observed in the axial mesoderm of A. mexicanus morphotypes may be the consequence of upstream events during gastrulation.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated by the authors.

claim: At equivalent stages, as judged by the percentage of epiboly, the advancement of internalized tissues migrating in the vegetal to animal direction is more precocious in cavefish embryos than in surface fish embryos.
source: At equivalent stages, as judged by the percentage of epiboly, we observed that the advancement of internalized tissues migrating in the vegetal to animal direction is more precocious in cavefish embryos than in surface fish embryos.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings presented earlier in the manuscript.

claim: Dorsal convergence and anteroposterior extension might be the driving forces that lead to the more advanced phenotype observed in cavefish gastrulas.
source: From the different measurements performed, we inferred that dorsal convergence and anteroposterior extension might be the driving forces that lead to the more advanced phenotype observed in cavefish gastrulas.
evidence: This is an inference based on the measurements of gene expression domains.

claim: The differences in hypoblast movements (relative to the percentage of epiboly) highlight the uncoupling of gastrulation cell movements and the epiboly itself.
source: Interestingly, the differences in hypoblast movements (relative to the percentage of epiboly) that we observed highlight the uncoupling of gastrulation cell movements and the epiboly itself, as spectacularly illustrated in the extreme example of annual killifish embryogenesis (Pereiro et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Pereiro et al., 2017.

claim: Temporal variations in gastrulation events might later correlate to differences observed in the off-set of dkk1b expression.
source: We suggest that these temporal variations in gastrulation events might later correlate to differences observed in the off-set of dkk1b expression, starting in cavefish before the 6-somite stage and in surface fish after the 8-somite stage.
evidence: This is a suggestion based on the observed temporal differences.

claim: The structural variations in the cavefish prechordal plate may relate to differential physical and adhesion properties of the organizer/prechordal cells in the two morphs.
source: Together with our observation of earlier movements of axial mesoderm cells in cavefish, these data suggest that the structural variations in the cavefish prechordal plate may relate to differential physical and adhesion properties of the organizer/prechordal cells in the two morphs.
evidence: This is a suggestion based on the observed structural variations and cited literature.

claim: Increased Nodal signaling and changed cell distribution have been reported in the organizer in cavefish embryos.
source: Moreover, increased Nodal signaling and changed cell distribution have been reported in the organizer in cavefish embryos (Ren et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Ren et al., 2018.

claim: The time of divergence between A. mexicanus morphotypes has been estimated to be recent (less than 20,000 years ago).
source: Regardless of the striking morphological evolution observed in A. mexicanus morphotypes, their time of divergence has been estimated to be recent (less than 20,000 years ago) (Fumey et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Fumey et al., 2018.

claim: The inter-fertility of the two morphs has allowed the use of hybrids for the identification of the genetic basis behind phenotypic change.
source: The inter-fertility of the two morphs, which reflects the short divergence time between them, has allowed the use of hybrids for the identification of the genetic basis behind phenotypic change (Casane and Rétaux, 2016; Protas et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Casane and Rétaux, 2016; Protas et al., 2006.

claim: The modifications in cavefish gastrulation are fully dependent on maternal factors.
source: Our analyses in F1 reciprocal hybrids demonstrate that the modifications in cavefish gastrulation are fully dependent on maternal factors.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the F1 hybrid data.

claim: 31.94% of the maternal genes that are expressed at the 2-cell stage have differences in transcripts levels between cavefish and surface fish eggs.
source: In line with this, RNAseq analyses showed that the RNA composition of cavefish and surface fish eggs varied greatly, with 31.94% of the maternal genes that are expressed at the 2-cell stage having differences in transcripts levels.
evidence: This statement is based on RNA-seq data analysis.

claim: Egg composition is a source of variation that can contribute to phenotypic evolution.
source: Together, these data strongly suggest that egg composition is a source of variation that can contribute to phenotypic evolution.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the F1 hybrid and RNA-seq data.

claim: The candidate genes beta-catenin 1 and 2 did not show significantly different levels of expression in RNAseq and qPCR analyses.
source: In both RNAseq and qPCR analyses, the candidate genes beta-catenin 1 and 2, which are involved in the establishment of the organizer (Kelly et al., 2000), did not show significantly different levels of expression (not shown).
evidence: This statement is based on RNA-seq and qPCR data, with a citation to Kelly et al., 2000.

claim: Two genes, oep and vsx1, which are implicated in the development of the prechordal plate, showed reduced transcript levels in cavefish compared to surface fish.
source: By contrast, two other genes, oep and vsx1, which are implicated in the development of the prechordal plate (Gritsman et al., 1999; Xu et al., 2014), showed reduced transcript levels in cavefish compared to surface fish.
evidence: This statement is based on RNA-seq and qPCR data, with citations to Gritsman et al., 1999; Xu et al., 2014.

claim: Ma et al. (2018) have recently described increased pou2f1b, runx2b, and axin1 mRNA levels in unfertilized cavefish eggs as compared to surface fish eggs.
source: Ma et al. (2018) have also recently described increased pou2f1b, runx2b, and axin1 mRNA levels in unfertilized cavefish eggs as compared to surface fish eggs.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Ma et al., 2018.

claim: These genes (pou2f1b, runx2b, and axin1) also show differential expression in our transcriptomic dataset.
source: These genes also show differential expression in our transcriptomic dataset.
evidence: This statement is based on the RNA-seq data.

claim: 6.5% of the 'top DEGs with fold-change >5' are involved in signaling.
source: Relevant to this work, we found that 6.5% of the 'top DEGs with fold-change >5' are involved in signaling (Figure 9C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 9C.

claim: Some of the signaling genes that are greatly modified are regulators of the Wnt pathway (i.e. sFRP2, dkk2, and wnt11).
source: Some of these genes are regulators of the Wnt pathway (i.e. sFRP2, dkk2, and wnt11) that are important for the establishment of the embryonic organizer.
evidence: This statement is based on the GO enrichment analysis of RNA-seq data.

claim: Members of other signaling pathways (i.e. FGF, BMP, and Nodal) are also greatly modified.
source: Members of other signaling pathways are also greatly modified (i.e. FGF, BMP, and Nodal).
evidence: This statement is based on the GO enrichment analysis of RNA-seq data.

claim: The origin of the induction of organizers with different properties in the two morphs might stem from an upstream maternally regulated event, with a domino effect leading to morphologically and functionally diverse brains.
source: Our interpretation is that the origin of the induction of organizers with different properties in the two morphs might stem from an upstream maternally regulated event, with a domino effect leading to morphological and functionally diverse brains.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the combined data.

claim: Both lens size and lens apoptosis are not under maternal genetic control when assessed at 24, 48, or 72 hpf.
source: In agreement with our previous independent findings at 36 hpf (Hinaux et al., 2017), but contrary to the finding of Ma et al. (2018), here we found that both lens size and lens apoptosis are not under maternal genetic control when assessed at 24, 48, or 72 hpf.
evidence: This statement is based on the F1 hybrid data and cites Hinaux et al., 2017 and Ma et al., 2018.

claim: There is little if any contribution of the maternal determinants on the lens defect and degeneration process in the cavefish eye.
source: From these results, we conclude that there is little if any contribution of the maternal determinants on the lens defect and degeneration process in the cavefish eye.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the F1 hybrid lens data.

claim: There is significant maternal influence on the developmental evolution of the anterior neural plate derivatives in cavefish.
source: Conversely, we show evidence of significant maternal influence on the developmental evolution of the anterior neural plate derivatives in cavefish.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the F1 hybrid data for retina and hypothalamus.

claim: Retinal morphogenesis control, including the typical cavefish coloboma assessed by the expression of Pax2a, appears to be maternally controlled.
source: First, retinal morphogenesis control, including the typical cavefish coloboma assessed by the expression of Pax2a, appears to be maternally controlled.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the F1 hybrid retina data.

claim: Dkk1b/Wnt signaling, itself fully maternally controlled from the beginning of gastrulation onwards, is involved in the retinal morphogenesis process.
source: We propose that Dkk1b/Wnt signaling, itself fully maternally controlled from the beginning of gastrulation onwards (Figures 1, 2 and 4) and whose manipulation affects the ventral eye phenotype (Figure 5), is involved in the process.
evidence: This is a proposal based on the combined data from Figures 1, 2, 4, and 5.

claim: The evolution of hypothalamic neuronal patterning, specifically the patterning of Hypocretin and NPY neurons, reflects a significant and long-lasting maternal influence.
source: Second, the evolution of hypothalamic neuronal patterning, specifically the patterning of Hypocretin and NPY neurons which begin differentiating around 20 hpf (i.e. long after zygotic genome activation) (Alié et al., 2018), also reflects a significant and long-lasting maternal influence.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the F1 hybrid hypothalamic neuron data, with a citation to Alié et al., 2018.

claim: Although maternal factors greatly influence early developmental decisions, later phenotypes become 'diluted' as other mechanisms enter into play.
source: As regards forebrain development more generally, our interpretation is that although maternal factors greatly influence early developmental decisions, later phenotypes become 'diluted' as other mechanisms enter into play.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the F1 hybrid data across developmental stages.

claim: As the zygotic genome takes control of development, allelic dominance has an increasing impact on the phenotypes after 15 hpf onwards.
source: We suggest that as the zygotic genome takes control of development, allelic dominance has an increasing impact on the phenotypes after 15 hpf onwards
evidence: This is a suggestion based on the F1 hybrid data.

claim: Retinal morphology at 2 dpf – the coloboma phenotype – is largely dependent on regulations that occurred in the mother's gonad.
source: it is remarkable that retinal morphology at 2 dpf – the coloboma phenotype – is largely dependent on regulations that occurred in the mother's gonad.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the F1 hybrid retina data.

claim: Hypothalamic neuronal patterning has very important behavioral and adaptive consequences.
source: The same holds true for hypothalamic neuronal patterning, which has very important behavioral and adaptive consequences (Alié et al., 2018; Jaggard et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Alié et al., 2018; Jaggard et al., 2018.

claim: Some behavioral traits in adult Astyanax have been shown to be under parental inheritance.
source: Of note in Astyanax, some behavioral traits in adults have already been shown to be under parental inheritance (Yoshizawa et al., 2012): the vibration attraction behavior and its underlying sensory receptors (the neuromasts) are under paternal inheritance in cavefish originating from the Pachón cave, whereas they are under maternal inheritance in cavefish originating from the Los Sabinos cave.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Yoshizawa et al., 2012.

claim: Besides Astyanax cavefish, only one study has reported a maternal contribution regulating the developmental trajectory of entry into diapause in a killifish.
source: To our knowledge, besides Astyanax cavefish, only one study has reported a maternal contribution regulating the developmental trajectory of entry into diapause in a killifish (Romney and Podrabsky, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Romney and Podrabsky, 2017.

claim: Astyanax cavefish appear to be a proper model in disentangling the very early genetic and embryonic mechanisms of morphological evolution.
source: Thus Astyanax cavefish appear to be a proper model in disentangling the very early genetic and embryonic mechanisms of morphological evolution.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the overall findings of the study.

claim: The modified expression of maternal genes could result from differential cis-regulation.
source: In addition, the modified expression of maternal genes could result from differential cis-regulation, which, to our knowledge, has not yet been explored for maternal effect genes in the evolutionary context in any species.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism underlying maternal gene expression differences.
